ai.description: *Protobothrops jerdonii* is a 70–90 cm pit viper. It features a dark brown body with yellow-speckled, black-edged dorsal blotches and a distinct, pale-striped head. It lacks a rattle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Protobothrops jerdonii* is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or orange-red vertebral stripe or series of blotches running along its dark, brownish body.
ai.habitat: *Protobothrops jerdonii* inhabits temperate forests and shrublands in the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellow Speckled Lancehead is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless among leaf litter or rocks to ambush passing small mammals and amphibians.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Protobothrops jerdonii* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a litter of 4–10 young. Mating occurs in spring, with births generally taking place in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Protobothrops jerdonii* is found in the Himalayas of Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters.
